title: Ensemble SLO Alarmer with Contextual Throttle for Canary Auto-Revert
creator: Lina Chen
description:
Problem statement: Canary rollouts and A/B tests currently rely on single-signal thresholding (p95 latency or error rate) which produces noisy, brittle auto-reverts during transient traffic shifts and synthetic probe flapping. We need an automated rollback trigger that reduces false positives, is cost-aware (token cost per request), and respects throughput and cohort size.

Proposal summary: Implement an "ensemble" SLO alarmer that fuses multiple signals (latency quantiles, error rate, token cost per request, throughput) using a weighted, confidence-aware voting mechanism. Add a contextual throttle that adapts sensitivity based on deployment stage (canary fraction), cohort traffic characteristics, and recent signal volatility. Combine this with adaptive hysteresis (multi-window confirmation), a cooldown backoff, and a synthetic-probe override path for sanity checks. The goal is to reduce unnecessary rollbacks by >=45% in our historical canary traces while preserving detection of real degradations within the same SLO windows.

Key innovations (how this is different from existing work):
- Ensemble weighting learned by backtesting historical rollout traces instead of fixed heuristics. We apply per-customer / per-model bias factors so that policies can be tuned for latency-sensitive vs cost-sensitive workloads.
- Contextual throttle: the threshold is scaled based on canary percent, cohort variance, and recent token-cost drift; e.g., a 1% canary with high token-cost volatility gets a more conservative trigger than a 10% canary with stable traffic.
- Bayesian confidence band for each signal: short-lived spikes with low posterior confidence are downweighted automatically.
- Cost-bias knob: teams can increase/decrease sensitivity to token-cost SLO violations to avoid rollbacks triggered by modeling changes that increase token usage but not semantic quality (or vice versa).

User stories / scope:
- As an SRE/ML engineer, I can create a rollback policy that references multiple SLOs and chooses a cost-bias profile.
- As a platform owner, I can run offline backtests against historical canary traces and receive recommended weights and hysteresis values.
- As a product owner, I can see per-policy explainability in Console: which signals contributed to a rollback decision and their confidence scores.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Complexity vs transparency: ensemble methods are more complex to explain. We will add explainability metadata and visualization in Console to mitigate.
- Training data bias: historical traces may underrepresent rare failure modes. Mitigation: include synthetic failure injections in backtests.
- Delay vs sensitivity: longer confirmation windows reduce false positives but increase MTTD. We expose cooldown and confirmation-window knobs to balance this per-team.

High-level design:
1) Signal ingestion: p50/p95/p99 latency, request error rate, tokens-per-request (avg & p95), throughput, synthetic probe health.
2) Per-signal scoring: compute recent-statistics windows (30s, 5m, 30m), estimate posterior deviation from baseline (z-score + Bayesian posterior), output score and confidence.
3) Weighting & fusion: multiply per-signal score by learned weight and confidence; sum to produce an ensemble alarm score.
4) Contextual throttle multiplier: final threshold = base_threshold * throttle(canary_percent, cohort_variance, cost_drift, deployment_stage).
5) Hysteresis & confirmation: require ensemble score > threshold for N windows (configurable) or until synthetic-probe fails.
6) Action: emit advisory, optionally trigger automatic rollback or staged evacuation based on policy (auto-revert, reduce traffic, or alert-only).

API & Console integration (proposal):
- Policy schema (Console + CLI): name, signals[], weights[], base_threshold, confirmation_windows, cooldown_minutes, min_cohort_size, cost_bias (low|medium|high), auto_action (revert|throttle|alert), explainability:true/false.
- Console UI: policy creation wizard with recommended defaults from backtesting; per-rollout explainability panel showing signal contributions and confidence bands.

Success metrics (KPIs):
- Reduction in unnecessary auto-rollbacks by >=45% on historical canary set.
- Maintain detection rate for genuine degradations within allowed MTTD budget (<5 minutes for P0 latency regressions at 10% canary).
- Adoption: 50% of new model rollouts using ensemble policy within 8 weeks of release.

Acceptance criteria: [list below]
acceptance_criteria: Backtest harness integrated: run ensemble policy on last 12 months of canary traces and produce recommended weights and hysteresis values.
Dashboard: per-policy explainability view in Console with signal contribution breakdown and confidence bands.
End-to-end flow: create policy via Console or CLI, attach to a canary rollout config, and exercise auto-action in staging with simulated degradations.
Failure modes: verify synthetic-probe override triggers immediate halt of auto-action during proven probe failures.
Performance: policy evaluation runtime < 50ms per evaluation at 1000 evaluations/sec aggregate (CPU bound path) or acceptable offload to a metrics-worker.
Telemetry: metrics emitted for decisions (score, threshold, action, contributing_signals) and audited in rollout timeline.
Safety: must include cooldown and minimum cohort size checks to prevent tiny cohorts from being auto-evicted.
Security: no sensitive customer data is stored in decision logs; only aggregated metrics and hashes of cohort IDs.
Regression baseline: auto-revert false-positive rate reduced by at least 45% vs existing single-threshold policy in backtests.
implementation_notes: Phase 1 (MVP): server-side evaluator implemented in runtime-controlplane; simple fusion (weighted sum) + fixed contextual throttle function + Console UI for enabling policies.
Phase 2: add learning pipeline to recommend weights using historical traces and simple Bayesian parameter tuning; backtest dashboard for policy candidates.
Phase 3: per-customer weight overrides, explainability improvements (counterfactuals), and ML-based anomaly detector as an optional signal source.
Data sources: metrics from Console metrics pipeline (Prometheus -> OLAP), synthetic probe results, rollout traffic metadata (cohort size, region, model-version).
Performance note: evaluation should be able to run synchronously in canary control loop; heavy backtests run offline via batch jobs on analytics cluster.
